Hi Lila — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a working draft that we can iterate on (Medverity_MAP_v0.9.xlsx) and an evaluation test pack with three representative vignettes (eval-test-vignettes.pdf). High level below — this is intentionally terse so the committee can read quickly.

Proposed success criteria (measurable):
1) Clinical concordance: >= 92% concordance with Medverity gold labels on the 150-case clinical vignette set (batch test).
2) Latency SLO: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for typical 512-token calls in your EU/US region (we can profile per-region).
3) Throughput resilience: linear degradation; system sustains 75 QPS for 60 minutes without error rate > 0.5%.
4) Data controls: all patient PII redaction rules applied; no raw customer data logged to persistent storage outside customer VPC.
5) Regression tolerance: no more than a 1.5% drop in key outcome metrics compared to baseline for reference prompts.

Exit gate definitions / fail severity (proposal):
- Blocker: any security/compliance gap (SAML/KMS missing), or clinical mislabeling incidence >4% on safety-critical vignettes.
- Major (fail for target cutover): mean latency > 500ms at 75 QPS, or error rate >2% sustained for 10+ minutes.
- Minor: UI/UX inconsistencies in admin console, or intermittent infra alerts that do not affect user-facing correctness.

Acceptance tests (runnable):
- Test A (Concordance): run 150-case gold set through MAP test harness; compute concordance and edge-case failure list.
- Test B (Latency & Throughput): synthetic load with representative prompt length distribution; measure p50/p95/p99 latencies.
- Test C (Security & Data): audit logs review, KMS key rotation test, and a table-level check that no plaintext patient fields are persisted.

Evidence artifacts we will deliver:
- Test run pods: raw logs + aggregated metrics CSV (evidence-checklist.csv attached)
- KV-cache/trace snippets for failed vignettes
- SOC2 audit pointer (for enterprise customers) and a short compliance checklist we supply for your auditors

Proposed cutover timeline (conditional on passing acceptance):
- Week 0: kick off MAP + data access for 2 weeks (test setup)
- Week 2: run acceptance tests and joint review
- Week 3: remediation sprint (if minor failures)
- Week 4: staged canary (1% traffic) -> 25% -> 100% over 7–10 days if no regressions

Next steps: if this matches what the committee wants I suggest a 30-minute review call with the clinical lead and procurement on Friday. I can update the MAP spreadsheet live during the call.

Thanks,

Lila / team — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Short answers and confirmations below; I'll bring the updated MAP and an evidence-runbook to the Friday call (10:00am PT).

1) Safety-critical vignettes: we will include a separate subset of 20 safety vignettes that are evaluated independently and flagged in the concordance report. These are part of the pack but scored and trended separately; any >4% failure on that subset is a blocker. (We'll include the SHA256 hash of the sealed vignettes in the evidence CSV.)

2) Latency profiling: we'll run the latency/throughput tests in us-east-1 as requested and provide a short variance note. We expect p95 in us-east to be +/- 30–50ms compared to west coast depending on network path; we'll profile with your staging endpoints so numbers reflect your network.

3) Rollback window: yes — operationally we support a 30-day staged rollback window post-cutover. Our runbook defines traffic-split steps and a safe rollback snapshot for model and routing configs. We'll include the procedural checklist in the evidence runbook.

Procurement licensing note: if cutover goes to 100% we will follow the committed reserved-capacity pricing in the draft SOW; I'll loop in our contracts lead next week if the committee signals intent.

See you Friday at 10:00am PT — calendar invite to follow.

Cheers,
